q: 1. Where is United Nations University located?
explain: The United Nations University (UNU) is headquartered in Shibuya, Tokyo, Japan.

2. Match the Group I with Group II and choose the correct answer.
**Group I:** (a) ICAO (b) FAO (c) IMF (d) ILO
**Group II:** (1) Canada (2) Italy (3) USA (4) Switzerland

q: 3. Which of the following UN agencies has its headquarters at Paris -----------
explain: The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) is based in Paris, France.

q: 4. Which of the following is not an agency of UNO?
options: International Committee of the Red Cross
explain: The ICRC is an independent humanitarian institution and is not part of the UN system.

q: 5. The headquarters of World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) is located in -----------
explain: WIPO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

q: 6. When ILO became a specialized agency of UN?
explain: While founded in 1919, the ILO became the first specialized agency of the UN in 1946.

q: 7. Which of the following UN agencies has received Nobel Peace Prize in 2020 A.D.?
explain: The World Food Programme (WFP) was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020 for its efforts to combat hunger.

q: 8. Which of the following agencies assesses the "LDC Graduation"?
explain: LDC graduation is monitored by the Committee for Development Policy (CDP) under the UN Economic and Social Council.

q: 9. In which Country, UNO has spent highest quantity of Budget?
explain: Historically, in the context of these specific records, Haiti has seen significant UN spending due to humanitarian and peacekeeping efforts.

q: 10. The mission to which nation has been declared as the UN's most dangerous Peace keeping Mission --------
explain: MINUSMA in Mali is frequently cited as the deadliest/most dangerous UN peacekeeping mission.

q: 11. When was the Convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women issued?
explain: The CEDAW convention was adopted by the UN General Assembly in 1979.

q: 12. As of August, 2024, there are ____ member states as the parties on UN convention against Corruption.
explain: As per the updated records provided, 191 states are parties to the UN Convention against Corruption (UNCAC).

q: 13. In which year, UN celebrated international peace on?
explain: The UN observed 1986 as the International Year of Peace, aimed at strengthening peace-related efforts worldwide.

q: 14. The United Nations General Assembly has declared 2023 as the -------
options: International Year of Fruits and Vegetables
explain: The UN General Assembly declared 2023 as the International Year of Millets to raise awareness of the health and nutritional benefits of millets.

q: 15. Which period was declared to mark as "World Decade of Indigenous Language" by United Nations?
explain: The UN declared 2022-2032 as the International Decade of Indigenous Languages to draw attention to the endangerment of many indigenous languages.

q: 16. Nepal was attained membership of UNO in ---------
explain: Nepal became a member of the United Nations on 14 December 1955, after its earlier applications were vetoed.

q: 17. When was Nepal elected to the UN Security Council as a non-permanent membership for the first time?
explain: Nepal first served as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council during 1969-1970.

q: 18. Who is the first permanent representative of Nepal to participate in UN General Assembly?
explain: Rishikesh Shah served as Nepal's first Permanent Representative to the United Nations after Nepal's admission in 1955.

q: 19. Who is the present permanent representative of Nepal in UN General Assembly?
explain: As per this reference material, Lok Bahadur Thapa is listed as Nepal's Permanent Representative to the UN.

q: 20. The first Nepalese prime minister to address UN general Assembly is ----------
explain: B.P. Koirala was the first Nepalese Prime Minister to address the UN General Assembly.

q: 21. When did Nepal participate in United Nations peace-keeping force as an observer for the first time?
explain: Nepal first participated as an observer in a UN peacekeeping mission in 1958.

q: 22. In which country did Nepal work as a peacekeeper for the first time under the United Nations?
explain: Nepal's first deployment as a UN peacekeeping troop contributor was in Lebanon.

q: 23. According to UN Peacekeeping Missions Report -2023, Nepal is the ____ largest troops Contributing Country in UN Peace keeping Operations.
explain: As per the 2023 UN Peacekeeping report referenced here, Nepal ranked as the top (1st) troop-contributing country.

q: 24. Of which organization among the following has Nepal become the member at first?
explain: Nepal's earliest membership among these bodies was with the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), joined shortly after independence-era engagement with the UN system.

q: 25. When was Nepal became the member of World Trade Organization (WTO)?
explain: Nepal became a member of the WTO on 23 April 2004, becoming the first Least Developed Country to join through full accession negotiations.

q: 26. Nepal first attained the membership of Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) in --------
explain: Nepal joined the FAO on 21 November 1951, prior to its UN membership in 1955.

q: 27. Who was the first Secretary General of SAARC?
explain: Abul Ahsan of Bangladesh served as the first Secretary-General of SAARC from 1985 to 1989.

q: 28. From which country, the concept of the rural Development bank was emerged?
explain: The rural development bank concept, notably the microfinance-based Grameen Bank model, originated in Bangladesh.

q: 29. Among the following South Asian Counties, Nepal first established diplomatic relation with:
explain: Among the given options, Nepal's diplomatic relationship with Afghanistan predates its ties with the other listed countries.

q: 30. Who is Current 4th Secretary General of BIMSTEC?
explain: As per this reference material, Indra Mani Pandey is listed as the 4th Secretary-General of BIMSTEC.
